jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Deductible
jokes.joke: I took my nephew to a skate park and told him, “I used to do this.” He handed me a board. One push in, my lower back seized so hard I had to lie flat on the concrete. The kids were impressed. They thought I’d invented a trick called “the deductible.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Grandpa Bails
jokes.joke: My grandpa, seventy-eight years old, took up skateboarding at the skate park down the street. I said, 'Grandpa, why now?' He goes, 'Doctor told me I need more cardio.' I said, 'He meant walking!' Grandpa just shrugged and said cardio's cardio. Yesterday he landed his first ollie and pulled his hip so bad he now does cardio in a waiting room, filling out forms with a hand that still smells like Bengay and victory.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Package
jokes.joke: Taking my seven-year-old to the skate park instantly turns me into a Secret Service agent. I don't even own a board. I just hover by the halfpipe in sunglasses, pressing a finger to my ear, whispering, 'The package is approaching the ramp. The package is attempting an ollie. The package has eaten pavement. Move in, move in... deploy the SpongeBob band-aids.'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Skate Park Detail
jokes.joke: I took my nephew to the skate park and went full Secret Service agent. Every time he hit a ramp I scanned for threats. He wiped out once and I body-slammed him shouting, 'Stay down, Mr. President!' He shoved me off and said, 'Uncle, it's just a board.' The other dads clapped. For him.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Skate Park Heroics
jokes.joke: I tried to be a hero at the skate park the other day. Some kid wiped out, and I jumped in like I was sacrificing myself for the greater good. I yelled, “I’ll save you!” and immediately tripped over my own board. The kid stood up fine, and I’m lying there like a martyr for absolutely nothing except my own bad decisions.

scores.comment: Clear premise and vivid closing image, but the route is predictable and slightly overextended.
Strong escalation, natural stage rhythm, and a clean final turn with the band-aids.
Solid physical escalation, though the final applause tag is weaker than the main image.
Understandable and compliant, but generic, repetitive, and lacking a distinct punchline.
Clean escalation, tight economical punchline that lands on a fresh word.
Strong sustained bit with good radio-speak escalation; SpongeBob band-aid snap is a nice bathos turn.
Fun visual but final line ('clapped. For him.') is a bit muddled and softens the punch.
Familiar 'clumsy hero' template; punchline mostly restates the setup rather than turning it.
Excellent economy and stage rhythm. 'The deductible' is a highly original and surprising punchline that lands with a great snap.
A competent story but slightly wordy and reliant on the familiar 'quirky grandpa' trope. The final image is decent but lacks a hard comic turn.
The premise is heavily telegraphed early on, and the 'other dads clapped' ending relies on a tired internet cliche rather than a fresh punchline.
Lacks a genuine comic turn. The joke merely describes falling down, and 'martyr' feels forced in as a literal description rather than a sharp observation.
Clean premise and solid final image; the deductible label snaps the health-failure bit into a real laugh.
Familiar old-guy-skates setup; mild payoff diluted by length and soft closing image.
Strong stage premise with escalating radio chatter that lands cleanly on the undercut band-aid line.
Clear self-own structure and usable martyr turn, but the trip is the expected route and the laugh stays mild.
Clean premise and a neat final turn; solid, mildly funny.
Warm and vivid but a bit long; payoff is gentle rather than sharp.
Strong stage rhythm and a fun Secret Service angle; good closer.
Clear premise but the turn is predictable; readable, modest laugh.
